documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Still walking. Fasting numbers 100-120, nothing under 80 on the meter. Endocrinology appointment set for late May. BP fine at home.
Exam: vitals as recorded; heart and lungs normal; no edema.
Plan: A1c/BMP. No changes. She'll ask endo about the insulin dose since sugars are tighter now.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, clinic visit 05/24/2023 (received 08/09/2023 in response to records request).

Interval history: Ms. Pagan returns for Cushing syndrome and type 2 diabetes. She has kept to her eating plan and her walking. For several weeks she has woken many mornings drenched in sweat with her heart pounding. No chest pain, no breathlessness, no recent illness.

Medications reviewed: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, lisinopril 10 mg daily, prednisone 15 mg daily. NKDA.
Family and social history unchanged: never smoker, social wine, administrative assistant.

Exam: BP 132/84, HR 78, BMI 29. General examination unremarkable.

Labs today: hemoglobin A1c 6.2%; fasting plasma glucose 72 mg/dL; creatinine 1.0 mg/dL; urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 25 mg/g.

Assessment:
1. Severe hypoglycemia: recurrent early-morning episodes on basal insulin, with A1c now well below target for her.
2. Type 2 diabetes.
3. Cushing syndrome on chronic glucocorticoid for lupus; steroid management remains with rheumatology.

Plan: reduce insulin glargine to 20 units at bedtime. Glucagon 1 mg kit prescribed; husband to be shown how to use it. Check fingerstick before bed and on waking for two weeks. Return in one year or sooner if lows persist.

documents.title: Insulin change
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just letting you know the endocrinologist lowered my night insulin from 24 to 20 because I've been waking up sweaty with my heart racing, she said my sugar is dropping too low early in the morning. She also gave me a glucagon shot to keep at home. Should I change anything else?

documents.title: RE: Insulin change
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update. Follow her new dose of 20 units. Nothing else changes for now. Check your sugar at bedtime and when you wake for the next couple of weeks, and for any reading under 70 take 15 grams of fast sugar (4 oz juice) and recheck in 15 minutes. Make sure your husband knows where the glucagon is. We'll get her note.

documents.title: Pharmacy fill and records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fill history shows glucagon 1 mg kit and glargine pens filled 5/25 under the endocrinologist. Our med list still shows glargine 24 units; left for PCP to reconcile once note arrives. Faxed records request to endocrinology for 5/24 visit note and labs.

documents.title: Endocrinology note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: May endo note arrived after a second request. Glargine 20 qHS, glucagon kit, A1c 6.2, fasting 72, creatinine 1.0, UACR 25. Med list reconciled. Messaged pt: she says the morning sweats stopped within about a week of the lower dose.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. No lows since the glargine went to 20 units in May; fasting now 120s-140s. Lupus quiet per pt. Periods still irregular.
Meds reviewed with bottles: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 20 qHS, lisinopril 10, prednisone 15, glucagon kit at home (unused).
PHQ-2 negative.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin intact. Feet: protective sensation intact, pulses present, no calluses.
Plan: fasting labs. Flu/COVID next month. Mammogram in December. Pap next due 2026. Colonoscopy due 2031. Eye exam overdue, she'll book.

documents.title: Flu and COVID vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza left deltoid and 2023-24 COVID right deltoid. No contraindications. Observed; fine.

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated fundus exam 11/01/2023. Acuity 20/20 OD, 20/25 OS corrected. Anterior segments normal. Posterior pole and periphery without diabetic changes in either eye. Assessment: diabetes mellitus type 2 without retinopathy. Return 1 year.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis compared to 12/2022. Scattered fibroglandular tissue. No suspicious abnormality.

documents.title: Screening mammogram
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Screening mammogram: BI-RADS 1, negative. Routine annual screening.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group, visit 02/20/2024.

Dear colleague, Ms. Pagan was seen for annual review of her systemic lupus erythematosus. No arthralgia, rash, mouth ulcers, chest pain with breathing or new hair loss. Examination: no synovitis, no malar or discoid rash, heart and lungs normal. Monitoring blood count and urinalysis in our clinic were within normal limits and renal function was stable. Lupus remains clinically quiet on prednisone 15 mg daily, continued. We will see her in 12 months.
Current medications per our record: prednisone 15 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, insulin glargine 20 units at bedtime, lisinopril 10 mg daily. NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Winter was hard to keep walking. Fasting 130s-150s, no lows since last May. Rheum letter in, no changes.
O: weight up a bit since fall. BP fine. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: T2DM on glargine 20, metformin. A1c today; if it climbs past the mid-7s we'll revisit the insulin dose carefully given last year's lows. Back to walking now the weather's turning. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Glucose test strips
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Insurance now requires PA for more than 100 strips per month. Submitted: T2DM on basal insulin with prior hypoglycemia, testing twice daily plus as needed. Approved through 6/2025. Pharmacy and pt notified by phone.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hypoglycemia without coma
conditions.note: no hypoglycemia since May 2023 dose reduction

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Feels OK. Weight has crept up again this year. No lows at all since spring 2023.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 20 qHS, lisinopril 10, prednisone 15 (rheum), glucagon kit.
PHQ-2 0.
Exam: BMI now just over 30, vitals otherwise as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft and nontender. Skin intact. Feet: monofilament normal, pulses palpable.
A/P:
1. Obesity, BMI 30.6. Added to problem list. Talked portions, evening snacking, and getting back to daily walks.
2. T2DM, A1c today. Hypoglycemia from 2023 resolved after dose change; removing from active list.
3. HTN on lisinopril, controlled.
4. Prevention: flu today, COVID in a few weeks. Mammogram December. Shingrix once she turns 50 in February.

documents.title: COVID-19 vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2024-25 COVID vaccine IM left deltoid. No issues during observation.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram, comparison 12/2023. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No suspicious mass or calcification.
